title: Introduce chronological fingerprint alignment and cohort resonance guard
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Adds a new canary guard (cohort resonance) that aligns per-window performance fingerprints across cohorts to reduce false-positive regressions during seasonal traffic shifts. Includes observability dashboards and a runbook.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a new continuous-canary component (chronological fingerprint alignment) and an associated rollout guard (cohort resonance guard) designed to reduce spurious alerts and failed rollouts during time-correlated workload changes (time-of-day, batch job windows).
Motivation: existing canary detectors trigger on short-term shifts that are correlated with temporal traffic patterns rather than code regressions. We observed ~18% of investigated alerts in Q1 were due to misaligned baselines across cohorts. This change stabilizes baselines by aligning per-window fingerprints and requiring cross-cohort resonance before triggering strong rollback actions.
What this implements:
- Chronological fingerprint alignment: builds compact per-window fingerprints (latency/throughput/skew histograms + token-size distribution) with exponential decay and aligns them across cohorts using DTW-like correlation and a small transform to compensate for known traffic skews.
- Cohort resonance guard: requires at least two independent cohorts to show correlated degradation in aligned fingerprint space before escalating to automatic rollback. The guard is parametrized with tunable sensitivity, minimum cohort size, and time-window hysteresis.
- Integration with canary orchestrator: the guard plugs into the existing canary evaluator chain as a pre-rollback gate. If the guard is uncertain it records a scoped annotation and opens an observability probe instead of immediately cutting traffic.
- Observability: new dashboards (fingerprint drift heatmap, cohort resonance score over time), new metric names: perf.canary.fingerprint_score, perf.canary.resonance_score, perf.canary.alignment_correction.
- Runbook and tests: a concise runbook (ops/runbooks/canary-cohort-resonance.md) detailing triage steps and a simulated traffic harness for unit and integration tests.
